canonical_statement: The primary objective was to determine cefazolin clearance during short daily hemodialysis.
Secondary objectives were to characterize cefazolin pharmacokinetics during SDHD and assess whether current dosing produced adequate serum concentrations.
This was a prospective, open-label pharmacokinetic study conducted at the University Health Network Toronto Rehabilitation Institute from February 2013 through November 2014.
The protocol received institutional research ethics approval and all participants provided written informed consent.
Eligible participants were adults at least 18 years old, noninfected, and receiving regular 2-hour SDHD six days per week.

inclusion_criteria: Noninfected: afebrile, no leukocytosis, no constitutional symptoms

canonical_statement: Participants were excluded for documented penicillin or cephalosporin allergy or cefazolin exposure within the prior 2 weeks.

canonical_statement: On study day 2, six blood samples and two dialysate samples were scheduled around SDHD and cefazolin dosing, with a final blood sample before dialysis on study day 3.
Figure 1 depicts two cefazolin doses on consecutive days with blood samples B1-B6 and dialysate samples D1-D2.
Cefazolin concentrations were measured by high-performance liquid chromatography; the assay variance was reported as 4%.
A one-compartment model with IV infusion and first-order elimination was used to estimate pharmacokinetic parameters for each participant.

Intradialysis and interdialysis elimination constants were derived from log concentration-time slopes, with clearance calculated as volume of distribution multiplied by the relevant elimination constant.
Dialysis drug removal was estimated from plasma concentration change and from dialysate recovery using trapezoidal area under the dialysate concentration-time curve.
An in-practice model simulated cefazolin infusion during the last 20 minutes of SDHD rather than immediately after dialysis.
The study compared observed and modeled cefazolin concentrations with a total-plasma threshold of 40 mg/L, derived from an 8 mg/L free-drug breakpoint and assumed 80% protein binding.

outcome.definition: Total-plasma threshold derived from an 8 mg/L free-drug breakpoint and assumed 80% protein binding

canonical_statement: Participant-reported adverse effects were monitored from cefazolin initiation through 2 weeks after the final dose.
Patient characteristics and pharmacokinetic variables were summarized with medians and interquartile ranges because the data were nonnormally distributed.
Median intradialysis cefazolin clearance was 1.95 L/h (IQR 1.66-2.45).

canonical_statement: Participants with RRF >1 mL/min generally had lower cefazolin concentrations than those with RRF <1 mL/min, but observed and modeled concentrations still met the 40 mg/L target off dialysis.
The study was limited by its small sample size of 10 participants.
Five of 10 dialysate sample sets were lost because of laboratory error.
Dosing conclusions were limited by the lack of pharmacokinetic analysis at steady-state concentrations.
The study measured total cefazolin concentrations rather than unbound free-drug concentrations.
Short sampling intervals may have limited accurate estimation of elimination rates; the authors noted population pharmacokinetic modeling would better address this issue.
Participants were noninfected, so dosing adequacy in patients with serious life-threatening infection was not established.
Large interparticipant variation in residual renal function and body mass index limited generalizability.
The authors concluded that cefazolin clearance during a 2-hour high-flux SDHD session was similar to clearance reported during 4-hour conventional high-flux hemodialysis.

The authors concluded that cefazolin 1 g during the last 20 minutes of SDHD or immediately after SDHD appeared adequate to maintain the study pharmacodynamic target for more than 90% of the dosing interval.
